property_summary: supportsInterface must return true only for the expected interface IDs (IERC165 and IAccessControl) and false for all others; the mutant always returns true, violating this for any non-matching interfaceId.

For any interfaceId that is neither type(IERC165).interfaceId nor type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, supportsInterface must return false; the mutant always returns true, breaking this for any such non-matching interfaceId.

For any interfaceId that is not type(IERC165).interfaceId or type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, supportsInterface must return false; the mutant always returns true, violating this for any such non-matching interfaceId.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true iff interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or the parent ERC165 supports it; the bug version always returns false, violating this for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId.

For any input, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true when interfaceId equals type(IERC165).interfaceId; the buggy version always returns false, violating this for interfaceId == type(IERC165).interfaceId.

For any input, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true when called on the contract itself (address(this)) since the contract has ERC165 and IAccessControl support; the mutant always returns false, violating this for the legitimate interfaceId values that the contract does support.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true if and only if the interfaceId is explicitly supported by the contract or its ancestors; the mutant always returns false, breaking this bijection for supported interfaces.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true if and only if it is a supported interface; the mutant always returns false, so it violates the requirement that the supported interfaces actually return true.

For any role and account, the reference C returns true only if the role is actually granted to the account, while the mutant always returns true, violating the invariant that an account without a granted role must see hasRole return false.

The reference AccessControl allows an admin to revoke a previously granted role, after which hasRole must return false for that account and role; the mutant always returns true regardless of revocation.

For any non-admin and non-proposer account, a scheduled and cancelled operation must not be executable by that account after cancellation even if hasRole always returns true; the reference correctly marks it done only when executed by authorized roles, while the mutant allows unauthorized execution.

For any role and account that is never explicitly granted, revoking that role must revert in the reference if called from the account itself, but the mutant allows renouncing a non-granted role without revert.
For any role, if an account has that role, renouncing it must revert if the caller is not that account; the mutant allows any caller to renounce on behalf of any account without revert.

For any role and account, the result of hasRole must be consistent with whether the account was previously granted or revoked that role; the mutant always returns false, breaking the rule for any account that has been granted a role.

For any address that has not been granted a role, hasRole must return false (matching the mutant), but for any address that has been explicitly granted a role, the reference returns true while the mutant incorrectly returns false.
For any role R granted to account A by an admin, hasRole(R, A) must return true after the grant; mutant returns false.
For any role that has been granted to any account, hasRole must return true for that role and account; the mutant breaks this by always returning false.
For any account granted a role by an admin, hasRole must return true for that role and account; the mutant always returns false, breaking the rule for any granted role.
The getRoleAdmin function must reflect the actual admin role stored for any role, but the mutant always returns bytes32(0) regardless of the stored admin role.
